name: GPS (Global Positioning System)
capability: 31 operational satellites, MEO orbit, global coverage, 1m civilian accuracy
strategic_value: Foundation of Western military and civilian navigation; all NATO precision-guided munitions depend on GPS signals
alert: Increasing GPS jamming and spoofing by Russia and China in contested zones

name: BeiDou Navigation Satellite System
capability: 45 satellites, global coverage since Jun 2020, sub-meter accuracy in Asia-Pacific
strategic_value: Eliminates China's dependence on US GPS; more accurate than GPS across Asia-Pacific; BRI partner nations shifting to BeiDou
tag: GPS KILLER — MORE ACCURATE THAN GPS IN ASIA
alert: Pakistan, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, and Thailand now use BeiDou for civilian infrastructure

name: GLONASS
capability: 24 satellites, global coverage, degraded accuracy post-2022 sanctions due to chip shortages
strategic_value: Russia's independent positioning system; critical for Kalibr cruise missiles and military operations in Ukraine
alert: Sanctions blocking replacement satellite components; constellation aging faster than Russia can replenish

name: NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation)
capability: 7 satellites (3 GEO + 4 IGSO), regional coverage 1,500km around India, 5m accuracy
strategic_value: Independent Indian Ocean navigation for naval operations; covers entire Indian Ocean Region including chokepoints at Hormuz and Malacca approaches

name: Galileo
operator: European Union Agency for the Space Programme (EUSPA)
capability: 28 satellites (24 operational + spares), global coverage, 1m public accuracy, 20cm encrypted
strategic_value: EU strategic autonomy from US GPS; encrypted Public Regulated Service (PRS) for government and military use independent of NATO

name: Starlink
capability: 7,000+ LEO satellites (as of early 2026), global broadband, proven battlefield communications in Ukraine since 2022
strategic_value: Transformed from commercial internet to geopolitical weapon; kept Ukraine connected during Russian invasion; US military now largest government customer
alert: Musk's control over activation/deactivation demonstrated during Ukraine counteroffensive — single point of failure for Western allies

name: SatNet / Guowang (China Star Network)
capability: Planned 13,000 LEO satellites; first launches 2024; designed to counter Starlink dominance
strategic_value: China's answer to Starlink; will provide independent broadband to BRI nations and PLA forces globally, denying US communications dominance in LEO
alert: Orbital slot competition with Starlink; race to fill LEO frequencies before spectrum is locked out

name: Yaogan Reconnaissance Constellation
capability: 100+ satellites (SAR, optical, ELINT), near-real-time global surveillance, carrier-tracking capability
strategic_value: Can track US carrier strike groups in real time; provides targeting data for DF-21D and DF-26 anti-ship ballistic missiles
tag: CARRIER KILLER EYES IN THE SKY
alert: Constellation grew from 3 to 100+ satellites in 15 years; now rivals US NRO coverage in Indo-Pacific

name: OneWeb
capability: 634 LEO satellites, global broadband, polar orbit coverage including Arctic
strategic_value: Only LEO constellation with full Arctic coverage; Bharti/India stake gives New Delhi space communications leverage; post-bankruptcy rescued from Russian control
alert: Originally launched on Russian Soyuz rockets; all launches shifted to SpaceX and ISRO after Ukraine invasion

name: Cape Canaveral / Kennedy Space Center
capability: Primary US launch site; 50+ launches/year; supports Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, SLS, Vulcan, Starship
strategic_value: Highest launch cadence facility on Earth; SpaceX alone launches more than entire nations; anchor of US space dominance

name: Baikonur Cosmodrome
capability: Soyuz and Proton rockets; historically 20+ launches/year, declining post-2022; only crewed launch site for Russia
strategic_value: Russia's primary launch facility; lease arrangement gives Kazakhstan geopolitical leverage; declining cadence reflects broader Russian space decay
alert: Kazakhstan increasingly hedging — signed space cooperation agreements with China and France

name: Wenchang Satellite Launch Center
capability: China's newest and largest launch site; supports Long March 5, CZ-8, future crewed lunar missions; 60+ launches/year nationally
strategic_value: Lowest-latitude Chinese launch site (most fuel-efficient); will launch China's lunar missions and Guowang megaconstellation

name: Satish Dhawan Space Centre (Sriharikota)
capability: India's primary launch site; PSLV and GSLV rockets; 8-10 launches/year; growing commercial launch market
strategic_value: Anchor of India's independent space access; launched Chandrayaan-3 lunar lander (2023); increasingly used by Western allies seeking non-SpaceX options

name: China ASAT Weapon (SC-19 / DN-series)
capability: Demonstrated kinetic kill vehicle in 2007 (destroyed Fengyun-1C at 865km); created 3,500+ debris fragments still in orbit; co-orbital ASAT tested 2013
strategic_value: Can destroy any satellite in LEO; 2007 test was strategic signal that China can blind US military in opening hours of a conflict
alert: 3,500+ debris fragments from 2007 test still threatening all nations' satellites in LEO

name: Russia Nudol ASAT System (PL-19)
capability: Direct-ascent ASAT missile; destroyed Cosmos 1408 satellite in Nov 2021 at 480km; created 1,500+ debris fragments
strategic_value: Demonstrated ability to destroy satellites in LEO; test forced ISS crew to shelter; signal that Russia retains space denial capability despite broader military decline
alert: 2021 test debris threatened ISS astronauts including Russians; universally condemned

name: X-37B Orbital Test Vehicle
capability: Reusable autonomous spaceplane; record 908-day orbital mission; classified payloads; can maneuver to inspect/approach other satellites
strategic_value: Classified military spaceplane with unknown full capabilities; suspected of testing space-based surveillance, satellite inspection, and proximity operations
alert: China and Russia cite X-37B as justification for their own space weapons programs

name: Schriever Space Force Base (GPS Ground Control)
operator: US Space Force — Space Operations Command
capability: Master control station for entire GPS constellation; manages all 31 satellites; backup at Vandenberg SFB
strategic_value: Single most critical ground node for Western navigation; if compromised, GPS accuracy degrades within hours; hardened against EMP and cyber attack
alert: High-value target in any great power conflict; redundancy exists but switchover is not instantaneous
